name: SwiftWyhash (WyRand)
verdict_reason: On an M4 Mac with -Ounchecked, filling a 100-million-element Double array with a wyrand generator took 65-81 ms against 3,318 ms with Double.random(in:), which uses the system generator. The algorithm is the one Lemire ported; the measured port uses newer upstream constants but the same operations.
tier_reason: Independent forum benchmark (hyperfine, M4, -Ounchecked, code posted in the thread), but it measures an updated port rather than this package as published.
claimed_speedup: About 50x faster than the default Swift random (65 ms vs 3318 ms for 100,000,000 Doubles; 81 ms when still going through Double.random(in:using:)), 42x in an earlier run; a second poster saw ~12x from swapping in a Mersenne Twister
workload: Fill a [Double] of 100,000,000 elements with uniform values in [0, 1); wyrand either fed through Double.random(in:using:) or converted directly by dividing by 2^64
one_liner: Pure-Swift wyrand generator; about 50x faster than Double.random(in:) with the system generator for bulk random arrays.
how_it_is_fast: Each value costs one 64-bit add, one 64x64-to-128-bit multiply and an XOR on a single UInt64 of state, with no locks and no system calls. SystemRandomNumberGenerator goes to arc4random_buf on Apple platforms and getrandom on Linux for every value, which adds locking and cryptographic mixing. The generator is a small struct that the compiler can inline into the fill loop.
use_it_when: Filling large arrays with random values for simulation, Monte Carlo or test data
Shuffling or sampling at high volume where predictability to an attacker does not matter
You want a seedable, reproducible stream
skip_it_when: Security-sensitive randomness (keys, tokens, nonces): wyrand is not cryptographically secure
Code that draws only a few values
caveats: The benchmarked WyRand is a forum poster's update of this package with newer upstream constants, not the package byte for byte
Part of the 50x comes from avoiding Double.random(in:) itself; through Double.random(in:using:) the gap was 41x (derived)
Single machine, single poster; Swift version not stated

Lemire's own follow-up post notes wyhash-style generators lose some of their edge on older ARM cores where the high half of a 64-bit multiply is slow; the M4 result suggests this does not apply to Apple silicon
tradeoffs: Not cryptographically secure; only 64 bits of state
The package lags upstream wyhash by several years, as noted in the thread
Small project (25 stars), no commits since May 2025

evidence.quote: The wyrand method was about 50x faster than the default Swift random.
grants me a ~12x speed increase in throughput
when filling a Double array of 100,000,000 elements. This was measured on an M4 Mac, compiling with -Ounchecked, and using hyperfine for the benchmark.
